chunks: What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

When you are an Imam, the taslim is only that you send salutation upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and say: “Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah.” Then when you have said that, the salat has ended.
Then you signal to the people and say, while facing the qiblah: “Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah, and His blessings.”
Likewise, when you are alone, you say: “Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah,” just as you gave salutation while being an Imam.

So when you are in a congregation, then say the same as you said, and give salutation to those on your right and your left. If there is no one on your left, then give salutation to those on your right, and do not omit the taslim to your right if there is no one on your left.

key_terms.التَّسْلِيمُ: the concluding salutation that ends the salat
key_terms.شِمَالِكَ: your left side, toward whom salutation is also given if present
key_terms.مُسْتَقْبِلُ الْقِبْلَةِ: facing the direction of the qiblah
key_terms.يَمِينِكَ: your right side, toward whom salutation is given

ai.seo_question: How should taslim be performed in salat according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the manner of taslim in salat for the Imam, the one praying alone, and the one praying in congregation. It clarifies the wording that concludes the salat and the additional salutation directed to those present.
